compute.reported_as: For the more challenging J2 = J1/8 model, we found that even deep GCNNs struggled to resolve the ground states of the 108- and 144-site clusters with sufficient accuracy (...) we used the residual GCNN architecture shown in Sec. II B, with 12 residual blocks of six feature maps. Instead of the standard SR step (7), we trained these very deep networks using a modified algorithm, dubbed LayerSR (...) In particular, we used 4096 samples until the energy plateaued, which took 4 days (approx. 600 steps), and then 16384 samples for an additional 8 days (approx. 300 steps). After training, we further improved the variational energies by applying a Lanczos step as described in Appendix D. All simulations were carried out on a single NVIDIA A100 GPU. || We compute sigma and mu3 by finding the local estimators (B1) of the operators H - <H> and (H - <H>)^2, labelled eps_loc and nu_loc, respectively, for 2^14 Monte Carlo samples

compute.reported_as: Appendix A9 Optimization parameters: We optimized all models using IT-SWO[25]. We used 30 iterations in the inner loop and chose imaginary time constant β based on the relative scale of the energy spectrum for different problems (Table V: Triangular N=108, β = 0.01). Each iteration was performed using adam optimizer[24] with b1 = 0.9; b2 = 0.99 and learning rate that was decayed exponentially with the rate of 0.1 over 8∗10^5 updates starting with 7∗10^−4 ... We optimized all GNN models for 8∗10^5 iterations (≈ 26000 IT-SWO steps). For larger system sizes we initialized the weights with values from smaller system sizes. ... All models were optimized using Google's Cloud TPU v4. All models trained within a day. ... Appendix A8b: All results were computed using MCMC using 2∗10^5 samples from equilibrated Markov chains. ... Appendix A8c: To measure computational efficiency we have timed the process of evaluating 7200 batches of 32 basis configuration within a MCMC process. The GNN-2 model took 17.4 seconds to accomplish this task, while our unstructured ResNet baseline finishes in 2.14 seconds. ... Appendix A6a: Node and edge functions of the Encoder, Processor and Decoder are implemented as MLPs with 3 hidden layers with ReLU activations. The node and edge embeddings have size 64, while hidden layers width 128. We use 6 message passing steps with residual connections in the Processor. || Sec. III Architecture: "The encoder maps nodes and edges of input graph X to latent features of width 64. Next, the processor performs M rounds of message passing, updating the graph as Gt = Gt−1 +GNt(Gt−1). The residual GraphNet blocks GNt [41] use MLP node and edge functions. The decoder computes the final latent edge and node features Y from GM, by processing them using a MLP." | "Nodes vi are initialized by concatenating c and s, and edges ejk between interacting spins are initialized to zero. The sublattice encoding s is a one-hot vector" | "we obtain scalar outputs by sum-pooling the latent features over nodes and edges; concatenating the results into a single vector Z of size 128; and processing it with a linear layer. ... (2) GNN-2, an ansatz which computes each output using a separate network with output size of one." || App. A6a: "The final linear layer maps 128-dimensional latent vector to 2(1) outputs for GNN(GNN-2) models." || App. A6b: "our selective experiments show that using shared weights in the processor module generally achieves similar performance to the unshared variation." || App. A7a Table III: Triangular "≤ 0.14" -> "Coplanar" (Fig. 8 'Coplanar' panel shows three colours) || App. A9: "During training we use the same MCMC parameters as for evaluation discussed in Appendix A2." || App. A2: "For efficiency we maintain a batch of MCMC chains, which evolves throughout optimization. We follow the rule of thumb of performing N MCMC steps between sampling from the chain to reduce autocorrelation effects, where N is equal to the number of degrees of freedom." (no chain count or batch size given)

compute.note: Row value matches the GNN-2 column of Table IV (separate amplitude/phase networks) for the 108-site triangular cluster. Blanket statements for all models: 8×10^5 Adam updates (≈26000 IT-SWO outer steps) on Google Cloud TPU v4, 'all models trained within a day' (an upper bound, recorded as wall_clock); number of TPU chips/cores not stated; larger systems were warm-started from smaller-system weights. samples = 2×10^5 MCMC samples used for the reported energy evaluation; the training batch/chain count is not stated numerically. No parameter count stated (architecture: embeddings 64, MLP hidden width 128, 3 hidden layers, 6 message-passing steps). Timing 17.4 s per 7200×32 evaluations is a relative-efficiency benchmark with unnamed hardware. || route2a kochkov-gnn (2026-09-24): parameters NOT counted. Stated: 64-wide node/edge latents, MLPs with 3 hidden layers of 128 + ReLU, 6 residual message-passing steps, decoder MLP, sum-pool of nodes and edges to Z of size 128 (so decoder outputs 64), final linear 128->1 per network, GNN-2 = two separate networks. Unstated, so no count: (1) whether processor weights are shared across the 6 steps (GN_t notation and A6b suggest unshared by default, but not said); (2) width of the zero-initialised input edge features; (3) LayerNorm or not (DeepMind encode-process-decode codes usually have it; the paper does not mention it); (4) whether the GraphNet blocks have a global block/features; (5) whether the one-hot sublattice vector has length 3 (Coplanar, Fig. 8) or a fixed padded length; (6) whether GNN-2's two networks are both full encode-process-decode stacks. Conditional evaluation for scale only (NOT a value): MLP(in) = 128·in+128 + 2·(128·128+128) + (128·64+64) = 128·in + 41408; per network = MLP(4) + MLP(1) + 6·[MLP(192) + MLP(128)] + 2·MLP(64) + 129 = 41920 + 41536 + 6·(65984 + 57792) + 99200 + 129 = 925,441; GNN-2 = 1,850,882 (unshared processor, 1-wide edge input, no LayerNorm, no globals); shared processor gives 306,561 per network, 613,122 for GNN-2; LayerNorm adds 2048 per network. Parameter count does not depend on N (all MLPs shared over nodes and edges; the sublattice one-hot is an input, not a learned per-site embedding), so the 36- and 108-site models have the same count for the same sublattice encoding. FLAG samples: 200000 is the Appendix A8b final-evaluation count ('All results were computed using MCMC using 2∗10^5 samples'); the per-step training sample count (number of chains/batch) is not stated; A9 only says training uses 'the same MCMC parameters as for evaluation discussed in Appendix A2', and A2 gives no number. The previous harvest reading (compute-harvest/fetched/parts/2110.06390.json) set samples null for this reason. Kept 200000 per rule 8 (no contradicting number), but it does not meet DATA.md's per-step definition; recommend null. FLAG iterations: 8×10^5 counts Adam updates (30 inner updates per IT-SWO outer step, ≈26000 outer steps); whether each update draws fresh MCMC samples or the 30 inner updates reuse one sample set is not stated, so iterations × samples may overcount sampling by up to 30×. The run was warm-started from a smaller-size model (A9: 'For larger system sizes we initialized the weights with values from smaller system sizes'); that pre-training is not counted. Table IV has a 36-site GNN-2 run at J2 = 0.125 (−0.5131(8)/spin), the likely warm start. || Ruling 2026-09-24: samples = 200000 is the final evaluation's count, not per optimisation step (DATA.md), so null.
